world.title: Sex-specific disease association and genetic architecture of retinal vascular traits in the UK Biobank
world.description: While sex as a biological variable has gained increasing attention in recent years, its effect in shaping retinal vascular phenotypes and their genetic architecture remains poorly characterized. Given known sex differences in vascular biology and disease risk, elucidating these effects may provide insights into sex-specific mechanisms of systemic vascular disease. Here, we investigated sex differences in retinal vascular phenotypes in the UK Biobank (N = 68k), which are emerging as non-invasive biomarkers for ocular, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative diseases. We used both interaction and sex-stratified analyses in disease association and genome-wide association studies, including the X chromosome. Our analyses identified sex-differential associations between retinal traits and cardiometabolic risk factors as well as disease outcomes. Several phenotypes showed prognostic relevance for mortality and cardiovascular endpoints in Cox models, predominantly in one sex, illustrating the limitations of sex-agnostic analyses. Genetic analyses indicated modest differences in genetic architectures, with females showing a greater number of associated variants and gene-level signals, and evidence for sex-specific trait–gene associations. These findings suggest sex-differential genetic and environmental contributions to microvascular morphology, possibly reflecting divergent biological pathways and risk profiles. Our study underscores the necessity of integrating sex-aware approaches in genetic and prognostic research to advance precision medicine and improve tailored risk stratification. Sex-stratified analyses of retinal vascular traits in the UK Biobank cohort reveal differences in disease associations, prognostic value, and genetic architecture, including an X-chromosome association for retinal vascular phenotypes.
